sourceType: Official Rajasthan Tourism website (Government of Rajasthan)
note: Facts extracted below; prose summaries in our own words, not copied verbatim from the source.
about: One of Rajasthan's oldest cities yet its most recently formed Rajput kingdom; traditions trace to ancient Viratnagar (~1500 BC), also called Matasya Desh, where the Pandavas are said to have spent the final year of their 13-year exile. Nestled in the Aravalli hills; forests are home to grey partridge, white-throated kingfisher, Bengal tiger, and golden jackal.

places.name: Bala Qila
places.facts: Built on the foundations of a 10th-century mud fort; marble columns and latticed balconies; six gates — Jai Pol, Suraj Pol, Laxman Pol, Chand Pol, Krishan Pol, Andheri Gate; accessible via Pratap Bandh forest entry to Jaipol; buffer-forest safari available. Fort entry 8am-3:30pm, safari 6am-4:30pm, closed Wednesdays.

places.name: Alwar City Palace (Vinay Vilas Mahal)
places.facts: Built 1793 AD by Raja Bakhtawar Singh; blend of Rajputana and Islamic architecture; marble pavilions on lotus-flower bases in the central courtyard; now houses the District Collectorate/government offices.

places.name: Government Museum
places.facts: Rare manuscripts including one depicting Emperor Babur's life, Ragamala paintings, miniatures, extensive armoury, across three large halls. Ticket window 9:45am-4:45pm.

places.name: Moosi Maharani Ki Chhatri
places.facts: Cenotaph for Maharaja Bakhtawar Singh and Rani Moosi; Indo-Islamic style; upper portion (columned pavilions, domed arches) in marble, lower section in red sandstone pillars; mythological/court-scene paintings and sculptures on the ceiling; nearby artificial Sagar lake with symmetrical stairs and towers.

places.name: Fateh Jung Gumbad
places.facts: Tomb combining domes and minarets on a square platform; dedicated to Fateh Jung, minister of Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan; medieval architecture example.

places.name: Purjan Vihar
places.facts: Garden conceptualised/built 1868 by Maharaja Sheodan Singh; includes 'Simla' (the Summer House) pavilion for shade.

places.name: Bhangarh
places.facts: 17th-century town built by Raja Madho Singh; legend of an evil magician's curse leading to its abandonment; widely called one of India's most haunted places. Entry sunrise to sunset.

places.name: Garbhaji Waterfalls
places.facts: Popular scenic waterfall spot for photographers and nature lovers.

places.name: Pandu Pol
places.facts: Hanuman temple at a spring/waterfall cascading from rock; legend ties it to the Pandavas' exile refuge. Entry only Tuesday, Saturday, and full moon days.

places.name: Jaisamand (Alwar)
places.facts: Artificial dam built 1910 by Maharaja Jai Singh; shaded pavilions and towers along the banks; scenic especially in monsoon.

places.name: Siliserh Lake
places.facts: Hunting palace built 1845 by Maharaja Vinay Singh for Queen Shila; now an RTDC hotel; boating available; winter birds and basking crocodiles.

places.name: Sariska Tiger Reserve
places.location: 200 km from Delhi, 107 km from Jaipur
places.facts: First tiger reserve in the world to successfully relocate tigers; declared sanctuary 1955, National Park 1979; closed Wednesdays.

places.name: Tijara Jain Temple
places.location: ~60 km from Alwar, on the Alwar-Delhi route
places.facts: Jain pilgrimage site built to commemorate the 8th Tirthankar, Shri Chandra Prabha Bhagwan, son of King Mahasen and Queen Sulakshana.

places.name: Moti Doongri
places.facts: Originally built 1882, main royal residence until 1928; Maharaja Jai Singh then demolished the old palace and built a grander one; now has gardens and city viewpoints.

places.name: Talvrakash
places.facts: Hot sulphur springs where pilgrims bathe; temple bells and langurs; associated with Mandav Rishi's penance.

places.name: Bhartrihari Temple
places.facts: Pilgrimage site tied to the legend of King Bhartrihari, said to have spent his last years here amid the hills.

places.name: Naraini Mata
places.facts: Hot springs and a temple to Naraini Mata; annual fair on Baisakh Sudi.

places.name: Neelkanth
places.location: Deep inside Sariska Tiger Reserve, ~30 km into the buffer zone
places.facts: Century-old northern-style temple cluster with Khajuraho-like carvings; remote, rough-road access; peacocks common; ~100m away stands a monolithic stone statue of Jain Tirthankar Shantinath.

places.name: Naldeshwar
places.facts: Old Shiva temple amid rocky hills with two natural ponds fed by surrounding hills; especially scenic in monsoon.

places.name: Neemrana Baori
places.facts: Stepwell resembling a fortress; 9 floors, ~20 ft each; no carvings (built later than the more ornamented step wells); colonnaded openings at ground level leading down to the water source.

places.name: Lal Masjid, Tijara
places.location: ~55 km from Alwar city, east of Tijara Town
places.facts: Red sandstone rectangular mosque with corner minars and arched doorways; three arched doorways opening into a hall that originally had three domes (southern dome collapsed); faint Arabic inscriptions on plastered surfaces. Entry sunrise to sunset.

places.name: Raja Bhartrihari Panorama Alwar
places.facts: Depicts the story of Raja Bhartrihari, ruler of Malwa who left his kingdom for spirituality, wandered the Alwar-Viratnagar forests, and became a disciple of Guru Gorakh Nath. Entry 10am-5pm, ₹10 adult / ₹5 child.

places.name: Veer Hasan Khan Mewati Panorama
places.facts: Dedicated to Hasan Khan Mewati ('Shah-e-Mewat'), who fought alongside Maharana Sanga against Babur at the Battle of Khanwa; includes a life-size statue. Entry 10am-5pm.

places.name: Hope Circus
places.facts: Circular heritage landmark inaugurated 1940, with stairs to the top from all four directions; close to the city's main markets.

howToReach.air: Nearest airport is Indira Gandhi International, Delhi, ~141 km; Jaipur International Airport ~166 km
howToReach.rail: Shatabdi Express from Delhi to Jaipur halts at Alwar
howToReach.road: Regular buses from Delhi, Jaipur, and Bharatpur
